metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Portugal

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Portugal using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of students within schools, and OECD typically provides sampling weights and replicate-weight information for variance estimation; however, this factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names or replicate method. The reported uncertainty statements (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that standard PISA variance estimation procedures were applied in the production of the database tables. For analysts reproducing these estimates, the recommended approach is to use the PISA-provided student sampling weights and the corresponding replicate weights (if available) when estimating means, shares, and differences, and to apply the PISA scaling/score construction procedures for the creative thinking scale.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking scale results and related associations; it does not provide an explicit methodological description of plausible values (PV) generation/combination or missing-data handling for the reported indicators. While PISA achievement scales are typically based on PVs, this factsheet does not state whether the displayed statistics are computed using PVs (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or alternative score representations, so PV handling cannot be verified from the text provided. Similarly, the factsheet does not report the missing-data strategy used in the OECD database tables, so missing-data handling is treated as a reporting gap for this extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Portugal in this factsheet is the set of 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading or science and for whom creative thinking results are reported in the PISA 2022 Database. The factsheet reports that 6,793 students in 224 schools completed the assessment in Portugal (representing about 96,600 15-year-olds), but it does not describe additional exclusions (e.g., item non-response thresholds) beyond the OECD’s standard PISA data processing.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports creative thinking outcomes for 15-year-old students in Portugal using the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test (32 open-ended tasks) administered in 81 countries/economies. Portugal’s mean creative thinking score is 34 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly higher than the OECD average (33). Performance is also described relative to mathematics and reading: Portugal’s creative thinking is above what would be expected from its mathematics performance and above what would be expected from reading performance, with a reported correlation of 0.7 between creative thinking and mathematics (and 0.7 with reading). In Portugal, 83% of students reach at least Level 3, and 29% are top performers (Level 5 or 6). The factsheet further highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status (9 score points between top and bottom quartiles) and gender (girls +2.1 points), and it reports that 36% of the variation in creative thinking is uniquely explained by mathematics performance. Methodological details on PV combination and missing-data handling are not provided in the factsheet text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It summarizes descriptive statistics, proficiency distributions, and reported associations from the OECD PISA database tables, without specifying any student-level predictive modeling pipeline, ML algorithms, or explicit PV/missing-data procedures in the provided text. Therefore, ML technique fields and structured ML findings are intentionally left empty, and the extraction focuses on the assessment design and reported benchmarks.
